newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge delays immigration law regulations.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge delays immigration law regulations.

text.p: A federal judge on Monday granted a request from immigrant rights advocates to delay the effective date for implementing regulations arising from a tough new immigration law.

Acting after a lengthy hearing, U.S. District Judge Emmet Sullivan ruled against the Justice Department just six hours before the law was due to take effect and delayed the regulations that would carry out the measure until April 5.

The law, approved by Congress and signed by President Bill Clinton in September, has sparked panic in some communities with large immigrant populations, creating long lines outside marriage bureaus and a steep rise in requests for a change in immigrant status.
The law's overall purpose was to tighten U.S. borders against illegal aliens. It also seeks to streamline deportation procedures, and the number of aliens exempted from deportation will be capped.

The lawsuit, filed by the American Civil Liberties Union and several other groups, charged the federal government failed to give immigrants the required amount of time to prepare for the law's sweeping policy changes.

The judge agreed, noting that the regulations governing the law's enforcement had been published on March 6. He said Congress in the law specifically required a full, 30-day period before the regulations could take effect.
